judged_text: When the token response lacks refresh_token — exactly the shape the sync-mode contract prescribes ('the response should only contain the access token and expiry date') — the code writes the literal string 'refresh_token' into the parsed data, which callers spread into the credentials they persist. On the first sync-mode refresh, office365-calendar and zoomvideo overwrite the user's real refresh token with the string 'refresh_token' inside the credential row, with no error raised at overwrite time; any later direct provider refresh posts refresh_token=refresh_token and receives invalid_grant, permanently killing the integration (re-auth required) once the real token is gone.

adjudication.rationale: The new helper `parseRefreshTokenResponse` unconditionally injects `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` when the parsed token payload lacks a refresh token (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts). In sync mode the minimum schema intentionally allows responses without `refresh_token`, so this branch will run. In `office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the returned data is spread into `o365AuthCredentials` (`{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }`) and then persisted via `prisma.credential.update`, which will overwrite the real stored refresh token with the literal string. This is a verifiable data-loss/correctness bug from the diff; similar usage exists in `zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts` where the same helper is now used for refresh parsing, making the overwrite risk plausible there too.
